why_angle: The cited What Hi-Fi pages carry no lab measurements, and the cited SoundGuys pages give only SoundGuys' own rundowns. None of them sets RTINGS' measured battery hours beside SoundGuys', and the two labs put Sony and Bose in opposite order. None gives the AirPods Max 2's measured 89.4% noise attenuation. This page sets both labs' battery results and SoundGuys' noise cancelling scores side by side for all six models.

page.title: Best Over-Ear Noise Cancelling Headphones (2026): Lab Battery and ANC Scores Compared
page.h1: Best over-ear noise cancelling headphones: what two labs measured
page.desc: Sony WH-1000XM6 vs Bose QuietComfort Ultra 2nd Gen, AirPods Max 2 and Momentum 4: SoundGuys and RTINGS battery rundowns and noise cancelling scores, side by side.
page.answer: Short answer. The best over-ear noise cancelling headphones in 2026 are the Sony WH-1000XM6: they tie the Bose QuietComfort Ultra 2nd Gen on SoundGuys' noise cancelling score (8.7/10), and their lowest lab battery result, 31.75 h at RTINGS, beats Bose's 27.2 h at SoundGuys.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Sony vs Bose, lowest lab result: 31.75 h − 27.2 h = 4.55 h more for the Sony.
  • How far the two labs disagree: Sony 37.23 h − 31.75 h = 5.48 h; Bose 37 h − 27.2 h = 9.8 h. Both Sony results are above 31 hours. Bose's results span almost 10 hours.
  • Bose's own test: Bose's footnote reports up to 24 h at 75 dB with full noise cancelling (18 h with Immersive Audio on), which is 30 − 24 = 6 h below its 30 h headline.
  • AirPods Max 2 vs Sony: 9.0 − 8.7 = 0.3 points more noise cancelling, for 385.6 − 254 = 131.6 g more weight (52% heavier) and at least 31.75 − 22 = 9.75 h less battery.
  • AirPods Max 2 vs Bose at the makers' stores today: $549 − $369 = $180 more.
  • Momentum 4 vs Sony at SoundGuys: 56.35 h ÷ 37.23 h = 1.5× the runtime, with 8.7 − 7.6 = 1.1 points less noise cancelling.
  • soundcore Space One vs Bose at SoundGuys: 42.95 h − 27.2 h = 15.75 h more runtime, with 8.7 − 8.0 = 0.7 points less noise cancelling.

Tight budgetsoundcore Space One (43.0 h, 8.0/10) {buy:soundcore-space-one}

What the labs measured, and where they disagree

SoundGuys plays music through each pair with noise cancelling on, peaking at 75 dB SPL, until the battery runs out. RTINGS runs its own continuous playback test (Test Bench 2.3). For three of these headphones the two labs roughly agree: AirPods Max 2 at 21.0 h and 22 h, Momentum 4 at 56.4 h and 62.3 h, and the Sony at 37.2 h and 31.75 h. For the Bose they don't. SoundGuys stopped at 27 h 12 min, RTINGS reached 37 h, and Bose's own footnote says 24 h. The Sony is the only flagship here that both labs measured above 31 hours with noise cancelling on. That is why it wins when the two noise cancelling scores are tied.

On noise cancelling, SoundGuys gives the Sony and the Bose the same 8.7/10, so battery, sound and price decide between them. The AirPods Max 2 measured highest: 89.4% of outside noise removed by perceived loudness and a 9.0/10 score, which beats 98% of over-ears SoundGuys has tested. The Marshall Monitor III A.N.C. cut noise by 83% on average (8.3/10). The soundcore Space One makes noise sound about one-quarter as loud at its strongest setting (8.0/10). The Momentum 4 cut low-frequency noise by about 75% (7.6/10), the weakest of the six. On SoundGuys' predicted sound score, the Sony leads at 4.8, ahead of the Bose at 4.7 and the Momentum 4 at 4.6.
